name: Avocado Toast with Poached Eggs
instructions: Toast bread slices until golden and crispy.
Mash avocado with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Rub toast with a halved garlic clove while warm.
Spread mashed avocado generously on toast.
For poached eggs: bring water to a gentle simmer with a splash of vinegar.
Create a gentle swirl in water, crack egg into center.
Poach for 3-4 minutes until white is set but yolk is runny.
Place poached egg on avocado toast, drizzle with olive oil, add red pepper flakes.
cooking_tips: Add vinegar to poaching water to help whites hold together.
Fresh eggs poach better than older eggs.
Add everything bagel seasoning for extra flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a side of fresh fruit or a small green salad.
storage_tips: Best eaten immediately. Avocado browns quickly when exposed to air.

name: Masala Omelette
instructions: Beat eggs well with salt and a pinch of turmeric.
Add finely chopped onion, tomato, green chili, and coriander.
Mix everything together.
Heat butter in a pan over medium heat.
Pour egg mixture into the pan, spreading evenly.
Let cook undisturbed for 2 minutes until bottom is set.
Fold omelette in half and cook for 1 more minute.
Serve hot with toast or bread.
cooking_tips: Beat eggs properly for a fluffy omelette.
Don't overfill — the omelette won't fold properly.
serving_suggestions: Serve with buttered toast and masala chai.
storage_tips: Best eaten immediately. Eggs get rubbery when reheated.

name: Overnight Oats
instructions: In a mason jar or bowl, combine rolled oats and chia seeds.
Add milk and yogurt. Mix well.
Add vanilla extract, cinnamon, and honey.
Stir until everything is well combined.
Top with sliced banana and berries.
Cover and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours).
In the morning, stir and add a little milk if too thick.
Add fresh toppings and enjoy cold or warmed up.
cooking_tips: Use at least a 1:1.5 ratio of oats to liquid.
Steel-cut oats need 24 hours soaking time.
Add toppings fresh in the morning for best texture.
serving_suggestions: Serve cold in summer or warm in winter. Top with nut butter for extra protein.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 5 days without toppings.

substitutions.milk: almond milk, oat milk, or coconut milk

name: Poha (Flattened Rice Breakfast)
instructions: Wash poha gently and drain. Let sit for 5 minutes until softened.
Season with salt, turmeric, and a pinch of sugar. Set aside.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add peanuts and fry until golden.
Add curry leaves, green chili, and onions. Cook until soft.
Add diced potato and cook covered for 5 minutes.
Add the seasoned poha and mix gently.
Cook covered for 3-4 minutes. Finish with lemon juice and coriander.
cooking_tips: Don't over-soak poha — it should be just softened, not mushy.
Use thick poha for best texture.
The sugar balances the sour-spicy flavors.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot with coconut chutney and a cup of chai.
storage_tips: Best eaten fresh. Can be refrigerated for 1 day.

name: French Toast
instructions: Beat eggs with milk, cinnamon, vanilla extract, and sugar.
Heat butter in a pan over medium heat.
Dip bread slices in egg mixture, coating both sides.
Place soaked bread in the pan.
Cook 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Repeat for remaining bread slices.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve with maple syrup.
Add fresh berries or sliced banana on the side.
cooking_tips: Use day-old or slightly stale bread — it absorbs better.
Thick-cut brioche or challah makes the best French toast.
Medium heat prevents burning while cooking through.
serving_suggestions: Serve with maple syrup, fresh berries, and whipped cream.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for 2 days. Reheat in a pan or toaster.
